propositions: The reconciler baseline is advanced from the pass-START snapshot before outbound is applied, so after rebar pushes a status change, the baseline retains the old value for exactly one pass, creating a false "local unchanged" condition

When a local status revert to a previous value occurs within the window after rebar's own outbound push and before baseline advancement, the suppression guard fires (local==baseline erroneously) and status is omitted from outbound, allowing inbound to overwrite with Jira's stale value
All five inbound-mirrored fields (summary/description/priority/status/assignee) share the same suppression-by-inbound guard and therefore share the same ABA vulnerability, not just status alone

Soft-failed mutations (unreachable state transitions, 400 comment-fallbacks, 404s) must not trigger baseline advancement because no sync actually occurred; advancing on pass-exit-code alone would mask genuine divergence

The ADR 0026 baseline is defined as the last-SYNCED value, not last-FETCHED; the fix overlays successfully-applied outbound mutations onto the fetch snapshot before baseline recording to restore the ADR's own definition
